chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad Al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who performs Ziyarah of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) [of the Messenger of Allah and Ali (peace be upon him)]?' He replied, 'It is like the Ziyarah of Allah on His Throne.' I asked, 'And what is the reward for one who performs Ziyarah of one of you (the Imams)?' He replied, 'It is like the Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), the like of this.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (specifically for spiritual merit, Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration to highlight the ontological elevation of the Ahl al-Bayt, where Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) equates visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with 'visiting Allah on His Throne,' a metaphor for proximity to Divine authority rather than literal anthropomorphism. This establishes the Imams as the ultimate locus of Divine presence, making their ziyarah a means of attaining nearness to God comparable to the Prophet's status.
